resale_co.name: Occupancy Permit (Change of Ownership) or Transfer of Ownership Permit (Certificate of Occupancy packet)
resale_co.lead_time: The City packet says all applications take 7 to 10 business days for processing and inspection dates; the City Code says Code Enforcement acts within 10 days of a completed application.
resale_co.valid_for: Not stated. If no certificate or permit is issued within 3 months of the application, the application becomes void. A temporary occupancy permit lasts up to 3 months.
requirements: Fire safety certificate (smoke alarms, CO alarms) from the Pleasantville Fire Department
Heat and hot water heater certificate from a licensed plumber or HVAC technician (electric units do not need one)
Fireplace certification if there is one: gas units by an HVAC technician or plumber, wood burning fireplaces by a licensed chimney sweep
All utilities on at the time of inspection

Home fit for habitation under the City Property Maintenance Code: no fire or accident hazards, adequate ventilation, light and sanitary facilities, no dilapidation, disrepair, structural defects or uncleanliness
Buyers using an LLC must give the owner's or property caregiver's name and contact information
Transfer of Ownership Permit only: a signed, notarized statement from the new owner taking responsibility for correcting the code violations found; this permit does not allow occupancy

fees.quote: For residential properties, a non-refundable fee of sixty dollars ($60.00) must be paid when application is submitted.

fees.label: Re-inspection, each
fees.quote: If a re-inspection is required to bring the unit into compliance a fifty dollar ($50.00) fee will be charged, and/or any additional inspections thereafter.

fees.label: Late cancellation (after 4:00 pm the day before)
fees.quote: Should you find it necessary to cancel an appointment, you must do so by 4:00 pm on the day prior to said appointment, or a fifty dollar ($50.00) fee shall be charged.

fees.label: Inspection aborted because utilities are off
fees.quote: All utilities MUST BE ON at time of inspection or the inspection shall be aborted and a $50 fee shall be required for re-inspection.

fees.label: Reprint after a name change within 5 days of printing
fees.quote: Should the current owner, new owners, tenant name, or name on application change within 5 days from when the Occupancy permit was printed, a new occupancy permit will be printed at an additional cost of $2.00

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Certificate of Occupancy packet from the City Forms page and complete the 'Occupancy Permit/Transfer of Ownership Permit' application (check 'Occupancy Permit - Change of Ownership', or 'Transfer of Ownership Permit' if the buyer will fix violations). Submit it to Code Enforcement (132 West Washington Avenue; mailing address 18 N. First Street) with the fee by check or money order payable to City of Pleasantville (no cash), plus the fire safety and heat/hot water certificates. Inspectors take scheduling calls from 8:30 to 9:30 am and 4:00 to 4:30 pm.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction/Zoning Official (Code Enforcement / Housing Division phone listed)

resale_co.notes: The City's Certificate of Occupancy packet (instruction page revised 11/03/23) says a Certificate of Occupancy is required before occupancy after any sale, and City Code §300-43 bars the sale or transfer of a dwelling unit until Code Enforcement has inspected it and a certificate of occupancy, occupancy permit or temporary permit is issued. Two paths exist: an Occupancy Permit for a change of ownership, or a Transfer of Ownership Permit, where the new owner signs a notarized statement taking responsibility for code violations; that permit does not allow occupancy, and the Code then requires a certificate of occupancy or occupancy permit within six months. Fee conflict: the City form charges $60 for any residential application, but the City Code fee table (§300-9, amended 9-6-2023) lists $60 for a residential occupancy permit and $40 for a residential transfer of ownership permit; confirm which applies. The Code text was read in full on ecode360. The application pages (updated 10/03/2022) name Kevin Cain as Construction Code Official; the City's current officials page names Ben Silkowitz as Construction/Zoning Official ((609) 677-4802), so he is listed, with the Code Enforcement / Housing Division number 609-484-3633. City staff emails are hidden behind Cloudflare email protection and were not recorded. Lead-safe certification and insurance apply to rentals only; yearly rental registration is a separate program. The City Forms page also posts a 'Land Use Certification Application' ($60), which is aimed at businesses (trade name, business owner) and is not listed as a resale item.

requirements: Homes built before April 4, 1991: smoke alarm on each level including the basement (not attic or crawl space) and near each separate sleeping area
Homes built after April 4, 1991: smoke alarm on each level and in each bedroom, 110-volt interconnected with battery backup
Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed (hardwired alarms excluded)
Carbon monoxide alarms in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas

Portable fire extinguisher: the 2025 application says it is required for multi-family properties only (excluding one- and two-family homes). The Fire Department web page still says extinguishers are required in 1, 2 and 3 family dwellings (page still lists it).

fire_cert.notes: The Pleasantville Fire Department is the local fire code enforcing agency (LEA code F). Its web page and 2025 application give the same fees ($60, $160 expedited). Phone numbers differ by source: the 2025 form gives OFFICE 609-569-2042 (used here), the Fire Department page lists the Fire Bureau at (609) 484-3625, and the City's CO packet and the state directory give 609-484-3670. The form also prints a cell number, which is not recorded. The state directory lists Abrown@pleasantvillefd.net for Anton Brown; the form's office email prevention@pleasantvillefd.net is used. The 2025 form excludes one- and two-family homes from the extinguisher requirement, matching the 2025 state law change (P.L.2025, c.19), while the web page text still lists 1, 2 and 3 family dwellings.

other_items.label: Fireplace certification
